newsitem.title: UK: McAlpine says enters 1997 much stronger.
newsitem.headline: McAlpine says enters 1997 much stronger.

text.p: British construction company Alfred McAlpine Plc has entered 1997 in a much stronger position than a year ago, chairman Sir Terence Harrison said.

"Across the group our prospects are improving, particularly in the new homes sector, and we are well placed to achieve a further improvement in performance leading to enhanced returns to shareholders," he said.
The company reported pretax profits of 11.2 million stg for 1996 before an exceptional item of 1.8 million. Net debt fell by 27.1 million, reducing gearing to 13.6 percent.
The policy of generating a higher quality order book and the decision to close the open tender traditional building business paid off, said Harrison.
The company focused on civil engineering, homes and special projects and its U.S. and slate interests.
Civil engineering recorded operating profits of 3.1 million, against 0.2 million after exceptional costs of 1.2 million in 1995, helped by a policy of winning higher margin work.
The homes division posted trading profit before an exceptional item of 9.1 million in 1996 down from 11.5 million.

The modest but steady improvement in the new homes market in the south east of England during the second half of 1996 has continued into 1997 and there is evidence that the gains being experienced are beginnning to benefit other regions.
